question: A thief started running at a speed of 12 m/s, after running for 10 sec a policeman started running to catch the thief in the same direction at a speed of 14.5 m/s. What is the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial distance covered by the thief in 10 sec = 12 × 10 = 120 m

Relative speed of the policeman = 14.5 − 12 = 2.5 m/s

Time required to catch the thief = Distance gap ÷ Relative speed

Time = 120 ÷ 2.5 = 48 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 48 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the thief = 12 m/s

Speed of the policeman = 14.5 m/s

Time for which the thief runs alone = 10 sec

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (in same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time to catch = Distance Gap ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by the thief in 10 sec = 12 × 10 = 120 m

⇒ The policeman starts running when the thief is 120 m ahead.

⇒ Relative speed of the policeman with respect to the thief = 14.5 − 12 = 2.5 m/s

⇒ Time taken by the policeman to catch the thief = 120 ÷ 2.5

⇒ Time taken = 1200 ÷ 25 = 48 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 48 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: SR = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
